title: OpenAEV content release manifest
description: List of the items of one release on one channel, with the hash of every archive. Serialised in RFC 8785 canonical form.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema the manifest follows.

repository.description: The repository the release comes from.

channel.description: edge for every release; stable for the releases recommended to everyone.

issued_at.description: The committer time of the commit the release is built from, in UTC: two builds of one commit give the same manifest.

release.description: The release's name: its date and a sequence number, YYYY.MM.DD.N.

payloads.description: Every payload version of the repository at the commit the release is built from, not only the ones scenarios use. The same limit as items.

release_approver.description: Added by the release job after the release approval. Absent from the build output; required by the verifier in an approved manifest.

semver.description: Semantic versioning; nine digits at most for each number.

github_login.description: A GitHub login in lower case: logins are case-insensitive, and a canonical case lets uniqueness count distinct accounts.

external_id.description: The scenario's identifier: a UUID in lower case, chosen once, that never changes from one version to the next.

version.description: The scenario's version, in semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

status.description: VERIFIED for a scenario in use; DEPRECATED for one replaced or no longer maintained; REVOKED for one that must no longer run.

name.description: The scenario's name, as the platform shows it.

description.description: What the scenario does and why, for a reader who decides whether to run it.

severity.description: How severe the threat the scenario reproduces is.

category.description: The scenario's category, as the platform classifies it.

main_focus.description: What the scenario mainly tests, as the platform classifies it.

platforms.description: A catalogue facet chosen by the contributor; it must include every platform targeted by an inject or step that needs an executor, which is checked against the export. At least one value, so that the scenario appears under some platform filter; for instance Generic for a scenario that runs on no endpoint.

threat.description: The threat the scenario reproduces: at least one of its CVEs, intrusion sets or techniques.

cves.description: CVE identifiers the scenario checks, such as CVE-2024-3400.

intrusion_sets.description: Names of the intrusion sets (threat actors) whose behaviour the scenario reproduces.

ttps.description: MITRE ATT&CK techniques the injects or steps play, such as T1595 or T1595.002.

type.description: time-based: injects run at set times. chained: the scenario is a workflow of steps, each starting at launch or when a step it depends on has run.

requires.description: What a platform needs to run the scenario.

openaev.description: The platform versions the scenario runs on, as a constraint such as >=3.261005.0.

edition.description: The OpenAEV edition the scenario needs: CE (Community) or EE (Enterprise). A chaining scenario needs EE.

injectors.description: Types of the injectors the injects or steps use, which the platform must have.

executors.description: Types of the executors the injects or steps need on the targeted endpoints, if any.

archive.description: The archive a platform imports, with its hash and size.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the archive, so that a platform can check it.

payloads.description: The payloads the scenario uses, each by its identifier, version and hash.

id.description: The identifier of the payload version: the payload_external_id of a file of payloads/.

version.description: The payload version the scenario uses: the version of a file of payloads/, which holds the payload's ID.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the payload's content, so that a platform can check it.

test_report.description: The report of the scenario's test run, by its hash and the release it belongs to; absent while releases carry no test report.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the test report.

release.description: The release the test report belongs to.

tabletop.description: Whether the scenario is a tabletop exercise, with no technical inject or step; a chaining scenario never is.

approvals.description: Who approved the scenario's change, and in which pull request.

pull_request.description: The number of the pull request that brought the change.

approvers.description: The people who approved the pull request, possibly none: a pull request merged without approval is said when the release is built.

payload_version.description: A payload version of the repository, with the file the release carries.

payload.description: The payload's slug: its folder in payloads/.

sha256.description: The payload hash of this version: the canonical content hash a platform recomputes.

openaev_id.description: The ID this version has in OpenAEV in V1 (its payload_external_id). Kept so that a platform that later stores versions can recognise it.

file.description: The version file, published next to the archives.

name.description: The file's name in the release: <payload>-<version>.json.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file's bytes. Kept beside the content hash because the file carries payload_domains, which the content hash leaves out.

size.description: The file's size in bytes, at most 262,144, the size bound of a version file.
